corrections.text: The article quotes Nicole Harris directly as saying no-provenance "is common for older releases and projects that have yet to configure Trusted Publishing," and that "such a release isn't necessarily malicious, since the missing attestation only means its origin can't be cryptographically verified." Help Net Security, the cited source, does not put either statement in quotation marks; both are the outlet's own paraphrase of Harris (linked to her PyPI blog post), not her verbatim words. The underlying facts are accurate; the quotation marks are not.
